title: Motion to lift speaking limits for the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill
what_it_is: A procedural motion moved by the Leader of the House, and assented to by the Speaker and Members present, exempting two office-holders from the Standing Orders so they may speak more than once and without time limits during the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill.
why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.

key_points.point: The Leader of the House asked for consent and general assent to exempt the proceedings from Standing Order No 48(3), so that Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann and Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng may speak more than once in the Second Reading debate.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: may I seek your consent and the general assent of Members present to move that the proceedings under discussion be exempted from the provisions of Standing Order No 48(3)

key_points.point: She also asked to be exempted from Standing Order No 48(8) to remove the time limits on those two speeches, saying their speeches may not finish within the time limit.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: I am asking to lift the time limit in respect of their speeches.

key_points.point: Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow will move the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill and will speak on the amendments on the Electronic Road Pricing 2.0 system and serious vehicular offences.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow will be moving the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill and will speak on the amendments pertaining to the Electronic Road Pricing 2.0 system and serious vehicular offences.

key_points.point: Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng will speak on the active mobility related amendments.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng will speak on the active mobility related amendments

key_points.point: Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann, on behalf of the Minister for Home Affairs, will speak on the new offences and increased penalties relating to speed limiters and other miscellaneous amendments.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann, on behalf of the Minister for Home Affairs, will speak on the new offences and increase in penalties relating to the speed limiters and other miscellaneous amendments.

key_points.point: The Speaker gave his consent to the motion.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker

key_points.point: The exemption was resolved: the proceedings are exempted from Standing Order No 48(3) so the two office-holders may speak more than once, and from Standing Order 48(8) to remove the time limits on their speeches for the Second Reading of the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: That the proceedings under discussion be exempted from the provisions of Standing Order No 48(3) to enable Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann and Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng to speak more than once for the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill

what_happens_next: The Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill proceeds, with Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow moving it, and with Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann and Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng able to speak more than once and without time limits.
not_said: What the amendments to the Electronic Road Pricing 2.0 system will change for drivers.
What the new offences and increased penalties relating to speed limiters will be, and when they take effect.
What the active mobility related amendments will change for users of paths and devices.
When the Bill, if passed, is intended to come into force.
